html:
A run of failed rains across the Sahel, the dry belt south of the Sahara, from the late 1960s to the mid 1980s. It was one of the longest and worst droughts recorded anywhere in the 20th century.

The worst years came in 1968 to 1974 and again in 1983 to 1985. Lake Chad shrank to a fraction of its size. Herders lost most of their animals, and the famine of the early 1970s killed tens of thousands of people, perhaps over 100,000, hitting nomads such as the Tuareg hardest. Many fled to towns and coastal cities. Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Chad, Upper Volta and Senegal all suffered.

The disaster made "desertification" a world issue. Sahel states set up a joint committee to fight drought in 1973, and the United Nations held a conference on desertification in Nairobi in 1977. At the time many blamed overgrazing and bad farming. Later research found the main cause was a shift in ocean temperatures, partly linked to air pollution from the northern hemisphere. The second wave of drought fed the Ethiopian famine of 1983 to 1985.
sum: A run of failed rains across the Sahel, the dry belt south of the Sahara, from the late 1960s to the mid 1980s. It was one of the longest and worst droughts recorded anywhere in the 20th century.
